expected.basis: NFC and NFD strings differ as opaque decoded identities.
A valid four-byte Unicode scalar compares by its decoded text.
A decoded NUL is an opaque character, not a C-string terminator.
Segment first, then decode; an encoded ampersand belongs to the identity.
A second question mark is query value text and an encoded hash is not a fragment.
Only the server-bound query contributes identity.
Only literal ampersands segment the query.
Only the first literal equals sign separates a key and value.
Once-decoded matching keys share one identity but retain original value spans.
Encoded aliases cannot evade conflicting repeated-value deferral.
A nonmatching malformed query name is not identity evidence.
Strict identity decoding applies to xsId, not unrelated opaque query fields.
An invalid nonmatching name cannot supply or erase a known xsId.
A literal plus decodes to a blank value before the empty-value test.
A whitespace-only field supplies no populated identity.
An invisible non-whitespace scalar is still part of an opaque ID.
One decoding pass leaves literal percent escapes, without recursive macro recognition.
Recognized raw percent macros are unresolved, rather than malformed percent encodings.
The exact installation placeholder stays unavailable after one decoding pass.
An overlong UTF-8 sequence is not a known identity.
A trailing percent sign cannot be treated as literal identity text.
Percent decoding requires exactly two hexadecimal digits.
Partial decoding must not silently retain a malformed suffix.
Malformed percent escapes precede invalid UTF-8 and unresolved macros in mixed repetitions.
Invalid UTF-8 precedes macro and empty-value deferrals.
Global trimmed URL dedupe does not erase separate caller memberships.
Session labels follow caller group order, while target rows follow original artifact order.
Caller labels remain string values, without object-key semantics.
Grouping comes from the caller, not campaign or placement identifiers.
A unique ad-session identifier is not made unique by a different route identifier.
The owner matcher accepts the UVP route family and does not declare a closed event vocabulary.
Host names are case-insensitive while opaque xsId values remain case-sensitive.
A trusted-looking hostname prefix cannot establish the exact owner matcher.
Userinfo text does not establish the endpoint host.
Parameter names are decoded only once, just like identity values.
The once-decoded uppercase X key is not lowercase xsId.
Distinct ordinary artifact kinds still provide equal observed session IDs.
An ungrouped neighboring row cannot become an inferred second session.
Only explicit membership contributes within-session evidence.
A literal value is not a cachebuster macro merely because it contains the word.
Hexadecimal escape case is irrelevant; decoded identity letter case is significant.
Known reuse survives an empty declared group, whose consistency check remains not evaluated.
The target span indexes original UTF-8 bytes before trimming or decoding.
Relationship targets carry each original row's metadata without aggregate occurrence rewriting.
An explicit owner selection cannot force nonmatching endpoints to become participants.
An exclusion continues to override an explicit allow selection, with core retained for ordinary document validation.
